bib.title: CROSSFIT: A Few-shot Learning Challenge for Cross-task Generalization in NLP
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 7163-7189

read.skipped: Reference list and the 160-row Table 3 task list skimmed only (data catalogue, not method).

question: Can a pre-trained text-to-text model acquire cross-task generalization from a set of seen NLP tasks (upstream learning) so that it learns unseen tasks better from few examples?
hypothesis: Upstream learning (multi-task or meta-learning) on diverse seen tasks improves few-shot fine-tuning on unseen tasks over direct fine-tuning; meta-learning is implicitly expected to do best since it targets rapid generalization.
contributions: The CrossFit Challenge: a problem setup standardizing seen/unseen task partitions, data access in each stage and the evaluation protocol
The NLP Few-shot Gym: 160 few-shot NLP tasks from open-access datasets in a unified text-to-text format, with a task ontology and eight partitions
Empirical analysis of multi-task learning, MAML, first-order MAML and Reptile on BART-Base, covering six research questions

method.summary: 160 Huggingface datasets are converted to text-to-text and few-shot sampled (16 per class or 32 examples, 5 seeds). A BART-Base model is first trained on a set of seen tasks (multi-task learning, MAML, FoMAML or Reptile), then fine-tuned separately on each unseen task's few-shot train set. Gain over direct fine-tuning of BART-Base is reported as Average Relative Gain (ARG) across eight seen/unseen partitions.
method.task: cross-task generalization / few-shot learning across 160 NLP tasks (classification, QA, conditional generation, other)

datasets.name: NLP Few-shot Gym (160 tasks from Huggingface Datasets)
datasets.size: 160 tasks; Dtrain = 16 examples per class (classification/regression) or 32 examples (other); Ddev same size as Dtrain; 5 random seeds so effective size 160 x 5 = 800
datasets.split: Dtrain and Ddev sampled from each dataset's original train set; Dtest = original dev set, or 20% withheld if no official dev split (sampled once before Dtrain/Ddev)
datasets.source: Huggingface Datasets (626 open-access datasets as of Feb 25 2021 in the pool); English monolingual only; excludes retrieval, sequence labeling, very long inputs
datasets.preprocessing: Unified text-to-text following T5, e.g. NLI as 'premise: <premise> hypothesis: <hypothesis>' with target entailment/contradiction/neutral; MRC as 'question: <question> context: <context>' with answer span target; QA formats also reference UnifiedQA

datasets.name: Partitions 2.1-2.3 (45cls, 23cls+22non-cls, 45non-cls)
datasets.size: 45 train tasks (all cls / half / none cls); 10 classification dev; 10 classification test
datasets.split: fixed test set of 10 classification tasks

datasets.name: Partition 3.1 Held-out-NLI
datasets.size: 57 non-NLI classification train / no dev / 8 NLI test

datasets.name: Partition 3.2 Held-out-Para
datasets.size: 61 non-paraphrase classification train / no dev / 4 paraphrase identification test

datasets.name: Partition 4.1 Held-out-MRC
datasets.size: 42 non-MRC QA train / no dev / 9 MRC test

datasets.name: Partition 4.2 Held-out-MCQA
datasets.size: 29 non-multiple-choice QA train / no dev / 22 multiple-choice QA test

datasets.name: Partition 5 Held-out-GLUE (PET experiment only)
datasets.size: non-GLUE classification tasks as train / GLUE tasks (8) as test

models.name: T5-v1.1-Base
models.init_from: pre-trained, C4 only (chosen over T5-Base which saw downstream tasks in pre-training)

other.note: Appendix D says 246M; Section 6 and Appendix C say 248M

training.objective: Upstream: seq2seq cross-entropy on source-target pairs from Ttrain (Dtrain and Ddev both used for gradient updates) via multi-task learning, MAML (one inner-loop step, theta' = theta - alpha grad L(Bsupport); outer theta <- theta - beta grad L(f_theta', Bquery), support batch from Dtrain, query from Ddev), first-order MAML, or Reptile (multiple inner steps, theta <- theta + beta(theta' - theta)). Downstream: fine-tune on each test task's Dtrain.
training.lr: Downstream few-shot fine-tuning: selected from {1e-5, 2e-5, 5e-5} on Ddev. Upstream lr (alpha, beta): null
training.batch_size: Downstream: selected from {2, 4, 8} on Ddev. Upstream: null
training.steps: Downstream: 1000 total updates, evaluated on Ddev every 100 steps. Upstream: null
training.hardware: Upstream: one Quadro RTX 8000 (48GB). Fine-tuning: one GPU from Quadro GP100, RTX 8000, RTX 6000, GeForce 1080 Ti or 2080 Ti depending on availability
training.compute: Upstream jobs finish within 3 hours on average; fine-tuning one few-shot task (with hyperparameter tuning over all 5 samples) takes about 4 hours on average
training.wall_clock: about 3 hours upstream; about 4 hours per few-shot task
training.seeds: 5 random few-shot samples (Dtrain/Ddev) per dataset; no further seed information

other.inner_loop_updates: limited to one for MAML/FoMAML due to memory constraints
other.second_order_on_larger_models: not possible with available compute, so only first-order methods used with T5-v1.1-Base and BART-Large
other.meta_learning_tuning: not tuned exhaustively; upstream hyperparameters (lr, batch, steps, optimizer, Reptile inner steps) not stated

inference.prompting: No prompting in main experiments (direct fine-tuning). PET experiment: top 3 patterns from Gao et al. 2020 per GLUE task, ensemble of the three models; variant 2 generates only the masked word.

metrics.name: Average Relative Gain (ARG)
metrics.definition: For each test task, relative change in its own metric after upstream learning vs. direct fine-tuning; averaged over all test tasks in Ttest

metrics.name: Per-task metrics (7 kinds)
metrics.definition: classification F1, accuracy, QA F1, exact match, Rouge-L, Matthew correlation, Pearson correlation, chosen per task

baselines: Direct fine-tuning of the pre-trained model on test tasks (ARG = 0%)
Multi-task learning vs. MAML, first-order MAML, Reptile
eval.protocol: Upstream stage may use Dtrain and Ddev of Ttrain tasks; Tdev used for validation only (no weight updates). Few-shot stage fine-tunes on Dtrain of each test task, tunes hyperparameters on Ddev, scores on Dtest. Averaged over 5 sampled few-shot splits. No significance tests stated.

availability.data: Datasets are public via Huggingface Datasets; the Gym is built from them (code in the repo)

evidence.quote: we limit the number of inner-loop updates to be one

results.claim: Multi-task upstream learning on the Random partition (120 train / 20 dev / 20 test tasks) gives the largest ARG, 35.06% over direct fine-tuning.
On the Random partition the meta-learning methods gain less than multi-task learning (MAML 28.50%, FoMAML 22.69%, Reptile 25.90%).
results.setup: BART-Base, Random partition, MAML (one inner step)
results.note: FoMAML 22.69%, Reptile 25.90% in the same row

results.claim: Held-out-MRC gives ARG 32.81% for multi-task learning, with meta-learning at 27.28% (MAML) and 28.85% (FoMAML and Reptile).
results.setup: BART-Base, train on 42 non-MRC QA tasks, multi-task learning

results.claim: Held-out-MCQA is the hardest transfer: multi-task ARG 12.20% and MAML only 4.69%.
results.setup: BART-Base, train on 29 non-MC QA tasks, MAML

results.claim: Across all upstream methods and partitions, about half of test tasks improve by more than 5% relative to direct fine-tuning.
results.metric: share of test tasks with >5% relative gain
results.setup: BART-Base, aggregated over upstream methods and partitions; 35.93% within +-5%, 12.60% below -5%

results.claim: Gains from multi-task learning and MAML on the same test tasks are correlated (Spearman 0.66, Random partition).
results.metric: Spearman correlation of relative improvement (MTL vs MAML)
results.quote: MAML is 0.66, with p value equals to 0.0015

results.claim: Training on only non-classification tasks helps classification test tasks as much as training on classification tasks (ARG multi-task 11.68 / 11.82 / 11.91%).
results.setup: BART-Base, multi-task learning, Ttrain = 45 non-classification tasks (2.3) vs 45 classification tasks (2.1: 11.68%) vs half-and-half (2.2: 11.82%)

results.claim: Enlarging upstream data per task up to 8x gives only a 4% ARG improvement, so more upstream data does not guarantee better cross-task generalization.
results.quote: stream data leads to only 4% improvement in ARG.

results.claim: Gains from upstream learning persist when 1024 target shots are available and fade with millions of examples.
results.metric: shots at which gain remains evident
results.setup: BART-Base checkpoints from Held-out-MCQA, MRC and NLI partitions; {32..4096} train examples plus full set
results.note: Appendix C says benefits extend to 2048 examples; CommonsenseQA outperforms direct fine-tuning even with the full dataset; MNLI gains diminish

results.claim: Test-task case studies show the same task gains differently depending on Ttrain, e.g. Race-High multi-task gain 26.71% (Random) vs 7.27% (Held-out-MCQA), and meta gain 6.59% vs -6.28%.
results.setup: BART-Base, Race-High as test task in two partitions
results.table: Table 2, row Race-High / Random, column delta multi

results.claim: Upstream learning can hurt tasks resembling the pre-training objective (Glue-COLA, Domain Crawl), attributed by the authors to catastrophic forgetting.
results.setup: Random partition, BART-Base (denoising pre-training); a conjecture, untested

results.claim: Pattern-exploiting training deteriorated average performance on BART-Base, with or without upstream learning.
results.setup: Held-out-GLUE partition; improved only on CoLA and MRPC; read from Fig 9, no numbers in text

results.claim: ARG worked example: +40% on one task and -25% on another averages to 7.5%.
results.setup: Illustrative T_A (50% F1 to 70%) and T_B (40% accuracy to 30%)

limits: Authors concede the ontology and partitions based on task format and goal are flawed, being only one aspect of task similarity.

Meta-learning uses only one inner-loop update (memory), is not tuned exhaustively, and is sensitive to hyperparameters and seeds; its weak results may reflect this, not an intrinsic limit. Training loss was unstable for FoMAML with T5-v1.1-Base.
Main analysis uses only BART-Base (139M); BART-Large and T5-v1.1-Base were checked only on the Held-out-Para partition with first-order methods.
No consistent pattern found for which Ttrain helps a given test task; upstream hyperparameters (lr, batch size, steps, optimizer) are not reported; no significance tests.
PET did not work with the encoder-decoder models used; cause is hypothesised, not tested.
Predates instruction-tuned large decoder models; models are small and tasks are few-shot fine-tuned, not prompted.

terms.definition: task-level generalization: how to learn a new task efficiently given experiences of learning previous tasks
a metric that computes relative performance changes before and after the upstream learning stage for each test task, and finally take the average across all test tasks
learning from the seen tasks Ttrain (with Tdev for validation only) before few-shot learning on unseen tasks

figures.caption: We present the CROSSFIT Challenge to study cross-task generalization in a diverse task distribution. To support this problem setting, we introduce the NLP Few-shot Gym, a repository of 160 diverse few-shot, text-to-text tasks in NLP.
figures.why: Two-stage pipeline (upstream learning on seen tasks, then few-shot fine-tuning on unseen tasks).

figures.caption: Experimental results for the CROSSFIT challenge with different task partitions.
figures.why: Per-task relative gains for each upstream method, showing variance across test tasks.

figures.caption: (Ttrain,Tdev,Ttest) partitions used in the study, and their ARG scores when upstream learning methods are applied.
figures.why: All eight partitions with ARG for four methods in one place.
